A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have defined an optimal protocol to efficiently transduce transplantable adult human bone marrow stem and progenitor cells using retroviral vectors.
we have developed a method for the efficient gene transfer of human BM CD34(++)CD38(-) hematopoietic cells in the absence fibronectin and with minimal prestimulation.

the use of a 6-day cytokine stimulation and virus exposure protocol, in the absence of any exogenously provided fibronectin, allows the efficient retroviral transfection of transplantable hematopoeitic stem cells from adult human bone marrow.
The main takeaway from our work is that
adult BM cells are as amenable to gene transduction as cord blood cells.
adult BM CD34+CD38- cells can be efficiently transduced with a single round of infection if they are prestimulated with cytokines and exposed to virus in tissue culture plates in the absence of FN.

the use of a cytokine combination that maximizes the mitogenic activity of CD34(+) cells in the absence fibronectin and the repeated exposure of these cells to virus can lead to the efficient retrovirus-mediated transduction of transplantable human bone progenitors in vitro and in vivo.
